learning: Verified precise negative: at Medium C128 BF16 decode with per-step cudaGraphLaunch on glm-a 15fd7f4/GB10, the host lane has no lever - GPU idle 0.68% steady-state in-span + ~0.06% inter-step, CPU hidden ~17x by the overlap scheduler; kernel time is 95.3% attention+GEMM. This independently extends g2-t2's C256 EAGER closure (99.2% busy) to the C128 GRAPH-REPLAYED regime using a real controller trace, so BOTH measured decode operating points are now host-lever-free; remaining decode levers are kernel-internal (attention/GEMM) which are reduction-order/precision-sensitive and out of frozen-BF16 scope absent a quality contract. The inter-step gap is itself 94% GPU-busy (eager sampler chain: embedding gather -> clamp_position -> argmax runs BETWEEN graph spans, not inside them) - a structural fact useful for future graph-coverage work: folding the sampler chain into the graph would target ~1% of the cycle, sub-noise. Method that worked: recompute-the-controller's totals FIRST (exact union match gates every downstream claim), then per-step/idle/composition slices, then an explicit assignment negative control for kernels outside annotation spans. Infra notes: GPU 'step' user annotations span only the graph kernels - sampler kernels fall in the gaps and are easy to miscount as idle; include gpu_memcpy/gpu_memset in coverage before calling anything idle.
